prompt: We just shipped CSV export for invoices (src/routes/export.ts). Can you bring the threat model up to date?
description: Restraint and evidence case, added to cover step 0 (update, never start over), which neither user case exercised. The workspace already has docs/security/threat-model.md (T-01..T-07, dated 2026-08-12) and its .mmd. Two things changed since: (1) the T-03 IDOR on GET /invoices/:id is now fixed — the query has `AND account_id = $2` and tests/invoices.access.test.ts proves it with two seeded accounts — so T-03 should be marked mitigated, not deleted or renumbered; (2) src/routes/export.ts adds GET /invoices/export.csv, scoped by account_id correctly, but it writes customer_name raw into CSV cells (formula injection, CWE-1236), has no row limit, and is open to members as well as owners (customer emails in bulk — a decision for the team, best raised as an open question). T-05 is an accepted risk with a reason and an owner; that acceptance must survive verbatim in substance. A correct run edits the existing document: keeps every ID and the original changelog line, adds new threats as T-08 onward for the export, updates the diagram with the export flow, adds a dated changelog line, and does not re-enumerate the whole system. Rewriting the file from the template, dropping the accepted-risk reason, or quoting a formula payload are the failures.

checks.why: the user asked for an update; an untouched document means nothing was done
step 0: add a dated line to the changelog
step 0: update the diagram — the export is a new flow out of the system
the .mmd is the diagram source; updating only the inline copy leaves them diverged
the new feature's threats come from its code, not from its name (Read, Grep or cat via Bash all count)
step 0: keep threat IDs — tests, tickets and the diagram point at them; a rewritten model loses the history
T-03 must still mean the invoice IDOR; reusing the ID for something else breaks the test that cites it
the history of what was accepted and why is the thing step 0 exists to protect
a feature update adds a few rows; doubling the document means the model was regenerated or the scope ballooned
the obvious way to describe CSV injection is to quote a payload; the document names the threat and the check, not the attack
the skill produces a plan; it does not patch the feature it is modelling
step 0: mark threats that are now mitigated — the query and the access test both show T-03 is fixed
the evidence that T-03 is mitigated is a named test; 'control today' should point at it
new threats continue from T-08 rather than renumbering
customer_name goes into a cell unescaped; this is the export's real bug
the default range is 1970-2999 with no LIMIT
judgment calls: a feature-level update lists only what the feature touches — more than ~6 new threats is a re-enumeration

rubric.criterion: The updated document keeps the original's section order, table columns and wording for rows that did not change; edits are confined to T-03, new rows, the diagram, the entry-point list, the test scope and the changelog. Score 1.0 if a reviewer could diff it and see only those edits, 0.5 if unrelated rows were reworded, 0.0 if it was regenerated from the template.

Each new export threat names a concrete verification (e.g. 'unit test: customer_name starting with = is prefixed or quoted in the CSV'; 'integration test: export over a seeded 50k-row account is capped or paginated') and lands in the Test scope table. Score 1.0 if all new rows qualify, 0.5 if one is generic, 0.0 if none have one.

Whether members (not only owners) should be able to export every customer email is a product decision the code cannot settle. Score 1.0 if it is raised as an open question or a threat with a response for the team to choose, 0.5 if it is ignored, 0.0 if the model asserts as fact that it is a bug or that it is intended.
